# Engine Simulator 2.0

Engine simulator for ECU testing (**Speeduino V0.4**) based on **ESP32-32U devKitC**.
The system connects to the ECU via the standard Speeduino 40-pin IDC connector and generates signals to simulate real engine operation.

## Architecture

### Signals generated by ESP32

| Signal | ESP32 Pin | To Speeduino | Method |
|:-------|:---------:|:-------------:|:-------|
| Crank Trigger | GPIO 12 | IDC Pin 25 | Square wave via hardware timer and level shifter 3.3V->5V |
| Cam 1 Trigger | GPIO 13 | IDC Pin 24 | Square wave via hardware timer and level shifter 3.3V->5V |
| Cam 2 Trigger | GPIO 14 | IDC Pin 24 (optional) | Square wave via hardware timer and level shifter 3.3V->5V |
| CLT (Temperature) | GPIO 26 (DAC2) | IDC Pin 19 | Analog voltage 0-3.3V, amplified to 0-5V |
| MAP (Pressure) | GPIO 25 (DAC1) | IDC Pin 11 | Analog voltage 0-3.3V, amplified to 0-5V |

### Manually controlled signals (potenziometri)

| Signal | Speeduino Pin | Notes |
|:--------|:-------------:|:------|
| TPS (Throttle) | IDC Pin 22 | 5V potentiometer, wiper/common to ESP32 ADC (GPIO 34) via voltage divider |
| IAT (Intake Air Temperature) | IDC Pin 20 | Potentiometer connected directly to Speeduino |
| O2 (O2 sensor) | IDC Pin 21 | Potentiometer connected directly to Speeduino |

### ECU input signals

| Signal | ESP32 Pin | From Speeduino | Notes |
|:-------|:---------:|:--------------:|:------|
| Fan Feedback | GPIO 27 | IDC Pin 15 | Fan status (0V = ON), 5V->3.3V voltage divider |

### ECU outputs monitoring

Speeduino outputs (injectors, ignition/coils, fan, idle, VVT, boost, fuel pump) are read by ESP32 via CD4050BE buffers for timing calculation (Phase 2).

---

## Firmware features

- **64 trigger wheel/crank patterns** (ArduStim compatible): 60-2, 36-1, 24-1, LS1, 58X, Chrysler NGC, BMW N20, GM 40-tooth OSS, and many others
- **RPM inertia model**: cranking 0->350 RPM, then idle at 850 RPM + (TPS x 6150), con low-pass filter
- **Start/Stop button**: starts engine with cranking ramp cranking, idle stabilization, gradual stop
- **Dynamic MAP simulation**: 100 kPa engine off, 85 kPa during cranking, 30-100 kPa based on RPM/TPS
- **Dynamic CLT simulation**: gradual warm-up, fan cooling, Newton cooling engine off
- **USB serial interface**: ArduStim protocol to configure trigger wheel/crank pattern and RPM mode from TunerStudio
- **Speeduino timing monitoring (Phase 2)**: input capture via ISR on 9 inputs CD4050BE (4 iniettori + 4 candele + fan) — measures injector on-time (ms), frequency, duty, ignition dwell e advance in degrees BTDC
- **WiFi AP + Web Dashboard (Phase 3)**: SSID `EngineSimulator2.0` / pass `1234567890` / IP `192.168.254.1`, responsive dashboard su `/`, allows selecting one of 64 trigger patterns e persisted to NVS at `/setup`, endpoint `/api/data` JSON

### Verification status

| Module | Status |
|:-------|:-------|
| Phase 1 — Crank/Cam generation and engine model | **Verified on hardware** (Speeduino/Mega2560 legge i giri; fix registri `GPIO.out_w1ts/w1tc` in ISR per core v3.3.x) |
| Phase 2 — Injector/ignition timing (input capture) | **Implemented and compiled successfully — hardware validation pending** |
| Phase 3 — WiFi AP + web dashboard | **Implemented and compiled successfully — hardware validation pending** |

## Hardware requirements

### Main components

| Componente | Quantity | Description |
|:-----------|:---------:|:------------|
| ESP32-WROOM-32U | 1 | Main microcontroller |
| 74AHCT125 | 1 | Quad level shifter 3.3V -> 5V (Crank, Cam1, Cam2) |
| TLV2372 | 1 | Doppio op-amp rail-to-rail (MAP/CLT buffers) |
| R-78E5.0-1.0 (RECOM) | 1 | Switching regulator drop-in 12V -> 5V, 1A, 91% |
| 40-pin IDC connector | 1 | Connessione a Speeduino V0.4 |
| CD4050BE | 2 | Hex buffer per ingressi ECU (iniettori/candele/ventola) |
| Trimmer potentiometers | 5 | (2kOhm x2, 10kOhm x3) — TPS, IAT, O2, etc |
| Push button | 1 | Start/Stop |
| DC barrel jack | 1 | Power 12V |

### Voltage levels

| Section | Voltage | Method |
|:---------|:--------:|:-------|
| Board power supply | 12V | DC barrel jack esterno |
| Logic supply | 5V | R-78E5.0-1.0 (switching, drop-in) from 12V |
| ESP32 and sensors | 3.3V | Regolatore onboard ESP32 |
| ESP32 digital outputs -> ECU | 3.3V -> 5V | 74AHCT125 |
| ESP32 analog outputs -> ECU | 0-3.3V -> 0-5V | TLV2372 (gain 1.5x) |
| Fan input from ECU | 5V -> 3.3V | Partitore resistivo |

## Build and Upload

### Prerequisites

- [Arduino IDE](https://www.arduino.cc/en/software) o [Arduino CLI](https://arduino.github.io/arduino-cli/)
- Pacchetto board **esp32** installato (`esp32:esp32` via Board Manager)
- Scheda selezionata: `ESP32 Dev Module` o `ESP32-WROOM-32U`
- Libraries for the dashboard (FASE 3) — use **ESP32Async** (compatible with
  core esp32 v3.3.x e mbedTLS 3; classic `me-no-dev` do not compile):
  - **ESP Async WebServer** (`arduino-cli lib install "ESP Async WebServer"`)
  - **Async TCP** (`arduino-cli lib install "Async TCP"`)

### Compile and upload

```bash
# Via Arduino CLI (prima volta: installa anche le librerie della dashboard)
arduino-cli lib install "ESP Async WebServer" "Async TCP"
arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32 firmware/Engine_Simulator_2.0.ino
arduino-cli upload --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32 --port COMx firmware/Engine_Simulator_2.0.ino
```

### Configuration

The trigger wheel/crank pattern can be selected:
1. **Dashboard web** (recommended): connect to WiFi `EngineSimulator2.0` (password `1234567890`)
   and open `http://192.168.254.1` -> page `/setup` to select the pattern (persisted to NVS)
2. **USB serial** (115200 baud): command `X` to select next pattern, `S<n>` to select by index
3. **ArduStim GUI**: desktop software connecting via serial to configure patterns and modes

## Project notes

- The **MAP sensor** integrato sulla Speeduino V0.4 (IDC Pin 11) cannot be used as an alternative to the DAC generated by the ESP32 for simulation. In this case, the MAP pin of the IDC must be connected to the PCB of the simulator.
- The **fan** is managed with feedback: Speeduino controls it, and the ESP32 reads it to model CLT temperature.
- The **IAT and O2 potentiometers** are purely manual and do not affect the simulation of the ESP32. They are used to test ECU corrections.
- The **KiCad PCB** (`Hardware/Engine Simulator 2.0/`) is complete: 2-layer routing with solid GND plane on B.Cu with thermal reliefs. DRC: **no clearance errors and no unconnected pads**; only cosmetic warnings remain (silkscreen text height and local footprint libraries are disabled). Updated DRC report in `Engine Simulator 2.0-drc.rpt`.

### Manufacturing outputs (Gerber + Drill)

Manufacturing files are generated with `kicad-cli` e ready for any fab house (JLCPCB/PCBWay/PCBcart):

- **`Hardware/Engine Simulator 2.0/Gerbers/`** — Gerber RS-274X, 9 layers (`F_Cu`, `B_Cu`, `F_Paste`, `B_Paste`, `F_Mask`, `B_Mask`, `F_SilkS`, `B_SilkS`, `Edge_Cuts`) + .gbrjob file `.gbrjob`.
- **`Hardware/Engine Simulator 2.0/Gerbers/`** — Separate Excellon drill files: `-PTH.drl` (plated holes, 0,3–2,2 mm) e `-NPTH.drl` (0 NPTH).
- **`Hardware/Engine Simulator 2.0/Engine_Simulator_2.0_FAB_gerbers.zip`** — ZIP archive of all Gerber/drill files, ready for direct upload to the fab house.

Board: **2 layers, 100×100 mm, thickness 1,6 mm, HASL**, min trace width 0,2 mm, min clearance 0,21 mm, min drill 0,3 mm (via) / 2,2 mm (M2 mounting holes, PTH connected to GND).
